scenario: AITA - For not extending a specific invitation to two nieces for an annual family event that everyone is invited to? | Every year, on the last day of March, we gather as a family to celebrate my father-in-law’s life at a specific restaurant. He passed away many years ago, and that was his favorite place to eat. My mother-in-law foots the bill as part of the celebration and everyone in the family that can attend is always welcome. Sometimes people bring friends and it is never a big deal and we all celebrate a great man. This year, we had 3 of the 4 of my mother-in-law’s kids and their families come and had a wonderful time. My wife took a picture and posted it to social media to honor her dad. The unrepresented kid (I say kid loosely as she is over 50) took exception to this and flew off the handle because their family didn’t get an invitation and were purposely excluded. It is an open invitation, and she and all her children are adults with working phones. AITA for not reaching out to them and explicitly inviting them? Or should they know they are welcome (since they have been every other year) and take the initiative to just come? I didn’t get an invite and I showed up, so maybe IATA for a different reason.

prediction.raw: A relatable scenario! I'd say NTA (Not The Asshole) for not extending a specific invitation to the niece. Here's why: 1. **Open invitation**: You mentioned that the event is an open invitation, and everyone in the family is welcome. This implies that there's no expectation of explicit invitations being sent to every single family member. 2. **Past behavior**: The niece and her family have attended the event in the past, which suggests they're aware of the tradition and the open invitation policy. 3. **Adults with working phones**: As you pointed out, the niece and her family are adults with working phones, which means they should be able to take the initiative to reach out and confirm their attendance or ask about the event. 4. **No malicious intent**: There's no indication that you or your family intentionally excluded the niece and her family. It seems like an honest oversight or a lack of communication. It's not your responsibility to personally invite every single family member, especially when the invitation is open and the event is well-established. If the niece felt left out or hurt, it's likely due to her own expectations or miscommunication, rather than any intentional exclusion on your part. That being said, it's always a good idea to be considerate and communicate with family members, especially if there's a large family gathering. A simple "Hey, we're having our annual celebration on [date] at [location]. Hope you can join us!" message would have sufficed, but it's not necessary in this case, given the open invitation and past behavior.
